Examples of foundational assistance include providing information on active study strategies, learning tools, and navigating medical school. Each student has a designated Learning Specialist who provides transitional support, such as developing a study schedule and adjusting to the volume and pace of learning in medical school. During more personalized meetings, Learning Specialists assist students with developing active study strategies and help them prepare for exams, including board exams. The program includes near-peer tutoring whereby 4th year students receive elective credit for providing 1:1 content support for both our curriculum and board exam preparation.

shortName: University of Nebraska College of Medicine
missionStatement: The mission of the College of Medicine at the University of Nebraska Medical Center is to improve the health of citizens of Nebraska by advancing health and biomedical sciences through the highest quality education, exemplary patient care and research excellence.
researchPrograms: Hundreds of research projects are underway at UNMC today, in bench science labs, translational research centers and clinical trials. Research opportunities are available for undergraduate students and medical students as well.
diversity:
There is support for students who demonstrate a sincere interest in working in under-served medical communities or reducing health disparities in under-represented populations and students from non-traditional backgrounds. 

https://www.unmc.edu/student-success/student-life/slido.html
https://www.unmc.edu/oce/engagement/index.html

shortName: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
missionStatement:
Our mission is to advance the health of all New Mexicans by educating and increasing the diversity of health professionals, leaders and scientists, providing outstanding and compassionate medical care, advocating for the health of all New Mexicans, and pursuing new knowledge, and excellence of practice.

Mission Impact in Admissions
• We observe mission-aligned selection practices when assessing applicants. Once minimum requirements have been met, we blind interviewers to the MCAT, GPA, and academic record of applicants. This allows us to select applicants who align with our mission and who are committed to improving healthcare in our local communities.
• We recognize the importance of rural and community physicians in addressing health equity issues. By involving them in our admissions committee they provide valuable perspectives to the selection process.
• In an effort to support applicants unsuccessful in gaining admissions, and/or from rural and underserved communities or low socioeconomic backgrounds, we provide a post application workshop, and individual consultations with specific recommendations to help individuals improve future applications. 

Mission Impact in Medical School Curriculum
• We provide students with the opportunity to engage in faculty-mentored scholarly projects related to health care issues in local communities. The focus on the Rural and Urban Underserved Program (RUUP) adds a significant dimension by allowing students to work directly with medically underserved communities. 
• The Practical Immersion Experience is a 6-week rural community-based clinical preceptorship, where students live in the assigned community. This provides a unique and immersive learning opportunity with first-hand experience to observe and understand daily life in a rural community, gaining insights into the specific community healthcare challenges and needs.
• Medical students participate in Learning Communities, which provide students with a support structure that includes a faculty mentor and upper classmates. This fosters a sense of community and mentorship, creating a supportive environment for students. 
• Incorporating Cultural Humility into our curriculum provides opportunities for students to learn about the populations they serve, such as teaching about use of birthing sashes in Navajo births and cleansing ceremony for local tribal and Native students. This approach enriches educational experience for students, and prepares them to provide culturally sensitive and patient-centered care.

Mission Impact in Medical School Student Support
• The HSC Center for Native American Health plays a pivotal role in addressing health-related needs and fostering collaboration within Native American Communities. Its specialization in various areas include; student and workforce development, community engagement, community-based participatory research, community health assessment capacity building, program planning, and project management.
• The Learning Environment Office mission is to foster an inclusive learning environment where teachers, staff, and learners thrive, and relationships are mutually respectful and beneficial to each other and to institutional climate. The initiatives, such as the speaker series, demonstrate a commitment to fostering respect, connection, and inclusion.

Mission Impact in Graduates
• 2025, UNM SOM ranked in Tier 1 for its Primary Care program in the US News and World Report. UNM SOM also ranked in Tier 3 for Research, and #23 for Most Graduates Practicing in Health Professional Shortage Areas
• Approximately 24% of all UNM-trained physicians are practicing in New Mexico
• UNM-trained physicians are practicing in 30 of New Mexico’s 33 counties
• 45% of all UNM-trained physicians practicing in New Mexico are in primary care specialties of Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, OB/GYN, or Pediatrics.
researchPrograms: Learning to think independently and scientifically when identifying and approaching medical problems are crucial skills that medical students must master. Each medical student at the UNM SOM is required to actively participate in solving a medical research problem with a research mentor. The scholarly project goal guides students to learn the process of applying the scientific method to solve health and medical problems, whether in the laboratory, clinic or community. The research requirements consists of two elements: 1) an experiential component where the student performs either a primary research, quality improvement project, or integrative review under the guidance of a qualified research mentor; and 2) a communication component where the student presents their research results in one of three ways: 1) oral or poster format, 2) paper, or 3) publication.
diversity: The UNM Health Sciences Center’s most important value is a steadfast duty to improve the health of all New Mexicans. We will serve our patients and the public with integrity and accountability. We will strive as an institution and as individuals to recognize, cultivate and promote all forms of diversity; to fully understand the health needs of our communities; and to advance clinical, academic, and research excellence. We are committed to perform our duties with compassion and respect for our patients, learners, and colleagues; and always to conduct ourselves with the highest level of professionalism.

shortName: New York Medical College
missionStatement: New York Medical College is a graduate health sciences university whose purpose is to educate physicians, scientists, public health specialists, and other healthcare professionals, and to conduct biomedical and population-based research. Through its faculty and affiliated clinical partners, the College provides service to its community in an atmosphere of excellence, scholarship, and professionalism. New York Medical College believes the rich diversity of its student body and faculty is important to its mission of educating outstanding health care professionals for the multicultural world of the 21st century. This commitment to diversity and inclusion is woven into the fabric of the institution.  Students come from across the US, representing a broad range of racial, ethnic, cultural, economic, and educational backgrounds.
researchPrograms: Basic science, translational, and clinical research opportunities are available through the NYMC Graduate School of Basic Medical Sciences, our clinical partners at neighboring Westchester Medical Center and the Maria Fareri Children's Hospital as well as the broad network of hospitals and research institutions throughout our catchment area in the tri-state (NY/NJ/CT) region.
diversity: New York Medical College believes the rich diversity of its student body and faculty is vital to its mission of educating outstanding and thoughtful health care professionals.  Diversity and inclusion are woven into the proud history of the institution and continue to be an essential component of its current-day mission.  The College seeks to admit a diverse class, including but not limited to diversity of gender, race, ethnicity, cultural and economic background, and life experience. The broad diversity of backgrounds and perspectives reflected in our community is integral to our humanistic values as a medical education institution in service to society.

shortName: NYU Grossman School of Medicine
missionStatement: At NYU Grossman School of Medicine, we strive to recruit and accept the most academically talented and interpersonally gifted student body, one with a collective ability and desire to deliver excellence in clinical care, research, and medical education to all members of society. The admissions committee strives to identify applicants we believe are poised to become tomorrow’s physician leaders. We are interested in applicants who are committed to meeting the needs of our patients, community, and the medical profession at large, as well as those prepared to thrive in our culture of excellence.
researchPrograms: All students participate in substantive research with world-class NYU Langone Health scientists and laboratories.  Students have a plethora of opportunities to carry out medically relevant research throughout their time at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, starting with their first year of medical school.  Students typically choose to pursue original, hypothesis-driven research in the basic, clinical, or translational sciences. All students participate in established Summer Research Fellowships (SRFs) between M1 and M2 years and continue research in later years, culminating in the completion of a scholarly product.

shortName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine
missionStatement:
The mission of the UNC SOM is to improve the health and well-being of North Carolinians and others whom we serve. We will accomplish this by achieving excellence and providing leadership in the interrelated areas of patient care, education, and research.

Our school’s mission informs the structure and content of our curriculum. Our curriculum reflects the ever-changing practice of medicine, meets the desire for early career differentiation and exploration, and promotes social justice as a cornerstone for equitable and safe healthcare.

Our school’s mission impacts student life and support services. Our student support bench is extensive to promote learning in a respectful and diverse environment.
 
We have an Advisory College system which provides a more accessible social and educational structure in the context of a large student body. 

Our Wellness Program includes group discussions surrounding stress, coping, loss, and more. One-on-one counseling, with therapists, provide services dedicated to medical students and increases access for our students. 

UNC SOM has a multipronged strategy to optimize the Learning Environment including enhanced reporting structures, robust incident management, bystander training, and intentional culture change.
 
Students arrive to medical school at varying points developmentally in their professional identity formation. The Student Professionalism Committee assures that students are educated and held to the highest standards of professionalism by addressing professionalism issues with an eye towards education and support rather than disciplinary action.
 
The Office of Academic Excellence (OAE) provides academic support for students across all training sites around the state. The OAE’s goal is to enable students from all backgrounds to be academically successful in medical school and prepared to pursue the careers of their choosing.

Our school’s mission influences admissions practices and priorities. To care for and represent our state and our nation, the UNC SOM recruits students from a variety of lived experiences to create a socially responsible highly skilled workforce. We not only wish to recruit primary care doctors and individuals who wish to practice in rural communities, but also recruit individuals who will be leaders in academia, science, and industry. We believe that interaction between students with varying clinical, research, and education interests enhances the experience of students at the UNC SOM. Particular programs that help us achieve our goals are described below.

The Community Health Track is a partnership that has grown from the pre-existing accelerated FIRST Program and the Kenan Rural Scholars Program. Leadership from FIRST and Kenan recognized the opportunity for collaboration and the creation of a dedicated track experience for students with shared interests, including rural and underserved care, commitment to the state of North Carolina, and the desire to work within Primary Care.  

The UNC MD-PhD Program prepares high-achieving students to be leaders in academic medicine and scientific health discovery. The primary goal of the MD-PhD Program is to train physician-scientists, fully capable of bridging the gap between science and clinical medicine. 

The Medical Educational Development program (MED) is a summer pipeline program for aspiring medical and dental students.

Our school’s mission is reflected in the professional activities of our graduates. After graduation, our students train in competitive residency programs at top institutions across our state and country ( https://www.med.unc.edu/ome/studentaffairs/residency-and-the-match/residency-placements/ ). Beyond residency, we are proud to see our graduates joining the faculty of top academic centers, as well as successfully practicing clinical medicine.
researchPrograms: UNC abounds with opportunities for research as medical students. Our well established MD PHD links 10 outstanding students per year with productive researchers across the full spectrum of disciplines, and our MD PhD students have the highest rate of independent funding for their PhD projects in the country. Our innovative MD MPH program gives interested students training in clinical epidemiology and population health, and up to a quarter of each class enroll. In addition to these formal programs, there are numerous other opportunities and a student research society. Almost 80% of students participate in some type of research experiences while at UNC, and most of these publish papers.

shortName: University of North Dakota School of Medicine and Health Sciences
missionStatement: The primary purpose of the University of North Dakota School of Medicine & Health Sciences is to educate physicians and other health professionals and to enhance the quality of life in North Dakota. Other purposes include the discovery of knowledge that benefits the people of this state and enhances the quality of their lives.
researchPrograms:
Leader in Rural Health
The School leads the nation in rural health through the Center for Rural Health. It is designated as the North Dakota State Office of Rural Health, a federal-state partnership that helps rural communities build their health care services through collaborations and initiatives with a wide range of partners across the state. 

Cutting-Edge Lab Facilities and Educational Space
The SMHS building opened in 2016 and is designed to facilitate the education of an interprofessional health care workforce necessary for the health and vibrancy of North Dakota’s population. It features cutting-edge lab facilities and educational space designed to foster active and collaborative learning. 
Research focuses primarily on neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Parkinson’s Alzheimer’s), epigenetics and infectious disease (e.g., Zika, avian flu, Ebola).
diversity:
INMED
Since 1973, Indians Into Medicine has assisted Indigenous students in pursuing a career in health care. Over 250 Indigenous physicians and over 500 Indigenous health professionals have graduated from UND as a result.

DIVERSITY STATEMENT:
The University of North Dakota and its School of Medicine and Health Sciences takes pride in their mission to meet the individual and group needs of a diverse and pluralistic society through education, research, and service.

shortName: Northwestern University The Feinberg School of Medicine
missionStatement:
Our mission is to impact the practice of medicine through discovery and education to improve human health. Our vision is to achieve this mission through continuous quality improvement.

The pursuit of excellence requires a learning organization grounded in leadership, innovation, and compassionate care that can translate new knowledge into better human health. These attributes are interwoven by professionalism dedicated to teamwork, collegiality, and social and intellectual curiosity. Such values promote the best interests of medicine and further strengthen our social contract with the community we serve.
researchPrograms: Feinberg offers several combined degree programs with a major emphasis on research (MD-PhD, MD-MPH, MD-MBA, and MD-MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics).  In addition, all students are encouraged to explore research interests.  Students participating in the Area of Scholarly Concentration will engage in a highly-mentored research project across all three phases of the curriculum. Complementing the AOSC curriculum and project, our competitive Research Intensive Scholarly Emphasis (RISE) program provides the opportunity for students (MD and MD/MPH) to spend an extra, funded year of mentored research during their training. Feinberg offers a broad range of research options including basic, translational, clinical, epidemiologic, educational, patient safety and health care policy. Learn more here: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/md-education/curriculum/components/learning-strategies/student-research/index.html
diversity: FSM is deeply committed to advancing healthcare for all. We strive to create a setting that allows students to influence the learning environment, challenge faculty and administrators, and explore and celebrate different backgrounds. Within our MD Program, we prioritize the importance of cultural humility in our training. Supported by our various clinical settings, we impart on our students that comprehensive care requires serving the individual patient’s unique needs, abilities, values, and challenges.  Our Office of Health Equity supports a number of programs for all students to explore, to become engaged in, and to develop. We also have initiatives to help students find community and mentoring so they can thrive at Feinberg.  For more info, please visit this page: https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/health-equity/index.html

shortName: Ohio State University College of Medicine
missionStatement: The Ohio State University College of Medicine seeks to recruit self-directed learners who are driven to become empathetic physicians providing evidence-based, compassionate medical care.  The Admissions Committee will assemble a class that displays diversity in background and thought, strong intellect, and the potential to improve people's lives through innovation in research, education, patient care and community service.
researchPrograms: Many first year medical students participate in the College of Medicine's funded research experience for the summer between Med 1 and Med 2. The College of Medicine also encourages and offers technical support for those students applying for off-campus, grant-based research, such as Sarnoff Fellowships or research at the NIH.
diversity: Ohio State’s College of Medicine recognizes that a class with rich and varied lived experiences promotes cultural awareness, understanding, and creates an appreciation for the importance of producing physicians who can better serve a robust community. The MEDPATH program’s aim is to increase the number students from educationally and/or socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds who enter medical school, and who show evidence of a commitment to practice in a medically underserved community. Visit https://medicine.osu.edu/education/medpath-program to learn more.

shortName: University of Oklahoma College of Medicine
missionStatement:
Our mission is to be the premier institution for advancing medical care, education and research in the state, and to be among the leaders nationally. Our goals are Uncompromising Quality, Exceptional Service, Innovative Education, Advancing Knowledge, and Institutional Strength.

Our Vision: To be a top-tier, research-intensive college of medicine
researchPrograms:
The Director of Medical Student Scholarship and their team of specialty-specific departmental directors (in Oklahoma City) and the Office for Research Development and Scholarly Activity (SCM) help connect students with research opportunities suited to the students’ current interests and future career goals. Summer research opportunities are also offered through several basic science and clinical departments and the Stephenson Cancer Center. The College of Medicine and the Student Council hold an annual Research Symposium to showcase student research.  

Explore OU College of Medicine Research: https://medicine.ouhsc.edu/about/research
Explore OU College of Medicine Symposium: https://medicine.ouhsc.edu/comresearchsymposium
Explore OU Tulsa School of Community Medicine Research: https://www.ou.edu/tulsa/research/school-of-community-medicine
Explore OU Health Sciences Research: https://linktr.ee/ouhscresearch
diversity:
The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine (OUCOM) is committed to advancing access at all levels. OUCOM recognizes that matriculating talented individuals from widespread backgrounds strongly benefits medical education, patient care, population health, and scientific discovery.

The Office of Access and Community Engagement (ACE) was created to further enhance its commitment to retaining a student body from varied backgrounds. ACE works closely with the University to enhance and preserve access for students and to cultivate meaningful relationships with the surrounding community through outreach initiatives. 

OUCOM directly manages the outreach and retention initiatives for its students by planning, implementing, and evaluating strategies to further a sense of belonging for all students, faculty, and staff.

https://medicine.ouhsc.edu/about/office-of-access-and-community-engagement

shortName: Oregon Health & Science University School of Medicine
missionStatement: It is the mission of the School of Medicine to enhance human health through programs of excellence in education, research, health care and public service to the larger community including underserved populations. In achieving these goals, the Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU) School of Medicine seeks to establish an educational environment that challenges its students to strive for academic excellence and fosters the development of compassion, humanism, professionalism, and cultural competence in the care of patients from their first days in the classroom to their final rotation in the hospitals and clinics. A fundamental priority throughout OHSU is to enable all students to fulfill their potential as human beings and as health care professionals while effectively meeting the health-related needs of the multiple communities they will serve.
researchPrograms: OHSU is the recipient of a Clinical and Translational Science Award from NIH. Centered in the Oregon Clinical and Translational Research Institute (OCTRI), the program is designed to develop innovative solutions to improve the efficiency, quality and impact of the process for turning observations in the laboratory, clinic and community into interventions that improve the health of individuals and the public. OCTRI has an embedded research training program open to medical student participation. Students may apply to participate in the experience which provides training for those interested in careers in clinical and translational medical research and the opportunity to participate in mentored research activities. The program has five-month and one-year research options; students participating in the one-year option will earn a Master of Clinical Research degree. After completing the experience, students will have taken the first major step towards a career as a physician-scientist.
diversity:
The undergraduate medical education program developed a new method of teaching medical students about the ways that social, economic, legal, and cultural structures impact health. During the fall semester, a course explores how issues such as immigration, gender, trauma, substance abuse, and racism affect patient care. OHSU’s SOM is one of the few U.S. medical schools teaching this unique course led by medical students.  A faculty-taught companion course covers such areas as cultural competency and implicit bias. Second-year medical students choose the topics, design, and lead six small-group sessions required for all first-year students.

General information may be obtained by contacting the Center for Diversity & Inclusion at cdi@ohsu.edu or https://www.ohsu.edu/center-for-diversity-inclusion . Additional information relating to School of Medicine diversity and equity opportunities for learners can be found online at https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/diversity-equity/learners .

shortName: Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania
missionStatement: The Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania will select students who are poised and prepared to become future physician leaders in health care. These students will serve their communities and contribute to society through their clinical, educational, research, health policy, and entrepreneurial efforts. Graduates of the Perelman School of Medicine will seek to advance care quality, science and discovery for the benefit of their local communities and the field of medicine more broadly. We strive to develop a highly talented student body with a breadth of personal and professional experiences that reflect these goals.
researchPrograms: Penn is an outstanding institution for research. Ranked among the top in the nation in NIH funding, there are well over 500 faculty members conducting basic and clinical research. Penn students tap into these resources in a number of ways: short-term elective research, scholarly pursuit, year-out programs with funding, a top MD/PhD program, and research-oriented MD/Masters programs. Read more about these opportunities at the following website: https://www.med.upenn.edu/admissions/dual-degrees.html

shortName: University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine
missionStatement:
Provide quality education for diverse and competent biomedical sciences researchers and physicians with the scientific, professional and ethical knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to provide excellent health services, with empathy and humanism, at the forefront of technology.
Generate new knowledge through biomedical, clinical, translational and community research to promote and seek solutions to local and global health problems.
Provide quality inter-professional health care services while contributing to the formulation of public policy in health sciences and education in Puerto Rico.
diversity: Please refer to our Diversity & Inclusion Policy in the following link: https://md.rcm.upr.edu/institutional-documents/

shortName: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine
missionStatement: Pitt Med's mission is to improve the health and well-being of individuals, communities and populations through cutting-edge research, innovative educational programs in medicine and biomedical science, and leadership in academic medicine. We strive to implement this mission with the highest professional and ethical standards.  Our commitment is to foster an environment that enables all students, faculty, staff and the communities we serve to develop to their fullest potential.
researchPrograms:
Since 1998, the University of Pittsburgh, led by the School of Medicine, has ranked among the top 10 recipients of National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding, underscoring its research stature. 

At the School of Medicine, areas of research focus include the biology of aging; neuroscience; vision and vision restoration; genome stability and tumorigenesis; vascular, developmental, structural, computational, and systems biology; comparative effectiveness research; immunology; cancer virology; and clinical research and clinical trials, among others.

As part of the curriculum, all medical students at the University of Pittsburgh engage in a mentored longitudinal research project, which provides traditional laboratory-based or clinical research training, as well as health policy, epidemiology, and comparative effectiveness research opportunities.
diversity: The School of Medicine is committed to maintaining a varied student body and community. We believe such diversity is invaluable in a case-based curriculum heavily based on small group and interactive learning. The school hosts a premedical summer enrichment program, the Prologue to Medicine Program, for admitted students who believe they would benefit from a preview of the medical school curriculum. Following admission, a broad range of support services and programs are available to enhance academic success.

shortName: University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry
missionStatement:
At the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry (URSMD) we improve the health of individuals and populations through an innovative medical education program that emphasizes humility and growth. We inspire learners to become compassionate leaders in medicine and science by emphasizing collaboration, discovery and excellence.

We are guided by the core principle of Meliora, meaning “Ever Better.” We are a medical school where individuals achieve their highest objectives, unhindered by constraints on access, creativity, or participation. Our students are exposed to new opportunities and perspectives. Through the Double Helix Curriculum, early clinical experiences and our revolutionary biopsychosocial model, developing doctors who see not only disease, but the entire person. Mentored research, international experiences, pathways and community outreach opportunities complement our curriculum. We foster the knowledge, skills, and behaviors of the physician/scientist/humanist and combine evidence-based medical science with the relationship-centered art that is URochester medicine's distinctive trademark.
researchPrograms: URochester offers multiple, diverse opportunities to conduct research at our internationally recognized institution. Research opportunities are available starting during the first year.  Students can take advantage of multiple funding opportunities for summer research between Phase 1 and Phase 2. Funding is available for a research year-out through our Academic Research track.  In addition to allowing students to perform longitudinal meaningful research, this enrichment program provides opportunities for students to engage in elective learning and discussion sessions that prepare our graduates for future training in an academic career. A research master's degree is available in some departments under this program.
diversity: URochester's Office of University Engagement and Enrichment seeks to create educational and programmatic opportunities through strategic collaborations for the University community to engage openly, learn continuously, and contribute meaningfully, while prioritizing respect, curiosity, well-being, and care. They focus on creating an environment that embraces a wide range of perspectives and ideas, that enhance learning, encourage critical thinking, and invite and deepen civil discourse to drive innovation, curiosity, and excellence.

shortName: Saint Louis University School of Medicine
missionStatement:
Mission and Values
The mission of the Saint Louis University School of Medicine is the pursuit of excellence in education, research, clinical care and community engagement through professional development, collaboration and social justice.

Core Values: 
Cura Personalis – Care for the whole person, rooted in the Ignatian principle that God created us to do good in the world, and embracing the humanity in all
Scholarship – Delivering transformative education and creating new knowledge
Discovery – Research, scientific inquiry, and the application of that knowledge
Equity – Striving for justice, fairness, and diversity in our education, research and service to the community
Collaboration – Partnership across Saint Louis University, SSM Health and the wider community 

Established in 1836, the school has the distinction of awarding the first medical degree west of the Mississippi River and proud to be part of the 450-year tradition of Jesuit education.

The School of Medicine trains physicians and scientists, conducts medical research, and provides health services on a local, national and international level. We strive to graduate physicians who manifest in their personal and professional lives an appreciation for humanistic medicine. Grounded in Jesuit values, we serve our community, which faces challenges of poor health indicators, education, poverty and racism and the School of Medicine continues to work for health equity and well-being of our neighbors. 

We embody Cura Personalis (“care for the individual person”). Our work goes beyond training physicians to be scholars of the human body. We graduate doctors who appreciate humanistic medicine, concern themselves with the sanctity of human life and commit to dignity and respect for all patients.
researchPrograms: Distinction in Research Award. Summer research opportunities and stipends are available between 1st and 2nd year. There are numerous research opportunities in both basic science and clinical departments.
diversity:
In keeping with our Ignatian Mission, the School of Medicine will be a place where everyone is welcomed, respected, and supported, so that we may be a community-responsive leader, working in partnership to reduce health inequities and improve the health and well-being of the St Louis region. The Saint Louis University School of Medicine is committed to the education of a culturally competent healthcare workforce.  We seek to immerse SLU's medical students and graduate medical residents in a training atmosphere that prepares them for the practice of medicine within the communities we serve.

Our focus includes:
- Strengthen recruitment/retention efforts
- Development and promotion of internal talent
- Create and support mentoring programs
- Offer education and training opportunities
- Increase collaboration between Saint Louis University School of Medicine and the St. Louis community
- Fostering the Jesuit tradition - agents of change who work to bring about a more just, humane world

shortName: Medical University of South Carolina College of Medicine
missionStatement: The MUSC College of Medicine is committed to developing outstanding physicians who will deliver the highest quality patient care with compassion and professionalism. Our students are equipped to be exemplary members of interprofessional teams and address complex needs of diverse populations. The educators and leaders at MUSC are committed to the advancement of scientific discovery, teaching and learning, and diversity and inclusion. MUSC graduates are highly competitive for matching into residencies and fellowships at prestigious institutions across the nation in a wide variety of specialties.
researchPrograms:
As South Carolina's only comprehensive academic health center, MUSC values research as an essential component in our overall mission to preserve and optimize human life in South Carolina and beyond, and provide an environment that promotes learning, discovery and healing.

MUSC COM medical students have a wide variety of research opportunities throughout the curriculum. The Medical Student Research Portal (MSRP) is a centralized portal for students to navigate research and funding opportunities and learn how to engage in a research project. 

The Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP) is available for undergraduate students. The program is offered through the MUSC College of Graduate Studies.  Information can be found on the Graduate Studies website at:  https://gradstudies.musc.edu/programs/pathway/summer-undergraduate-research-program.
diversity:
The MUSC College of Medicine PRIME Division offers nationally recognized programs to support underrepresented students pursuing a career in medicine. We aim to create an environment that fosters cultural understanding, cultural competency, and opportunities for all backgrounds. 

We offer programs and initiatives to support students from varied backgrounds interested in pursuing a career in medicine, including students with disabilities, those from rural backgrounds, first-generation college students, those from disadvantaged or marginalized backgrounds, and other students interested in addressing health disparities in the communities they serve.  

Our different pathway programs are as follows:

Students Mentors and Mentees in Medicine (SM3)
Summer Institute
Summer Medicine Academy
Post-Baccalaureate Reapplication Program (PREP)

https://medicine.musc.edu/about/pathways-engagement

shortName: University of South Dakota, Sanford School of Medicine
missionStatement:
The mission of the University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine is to provide the opportunity for South Dakota residents to receive a quality, broad-based medical education with an emphasis on family medicine.  The curriculum is to be established to encourage graduates to serve people living in the medically underserved areas of South Dakota and is to require excellence in the basic sciences and in all clinical disciplines.

The University of South Dakota Sanford School of Medicine is to provide to its students and to the people of South Dakota excellence in education, research and service.  To these ends, the School is to provide educational pathways leading to both the Doctor of Medicine and the Doctor of Philosophy Degrees. Quality health care for the people of South Dakota is addressed by undergraduate, graduate and continuing educational programs as well as by basic and applied medical research.  The Sanford School of Medicine should serve as a technical resource in the development of health care policy in the state and provide extension and research initiatives to improve the health care of the citizens of the state.
researchPrograms: Basic, clinical and translational research opportunities are available for interested students.  The school also has an MD/PhD dual degree program as well as a Scholarship Pathways Program with an opportunity for research as well as educational or service programs.
diversity: The Sanford School of Medicine is committed to training a diverse group of students to meet the needs of the diverse population of the state.  Applicants may contact the Associate Dean for Community Health and Engagement for further information. In addition, we have a robust Academic Success program which includes one-on-one support with learning specialists, peer tutoring and student-led supplemental instruction sessions.

shortName: Keck School of Medicine of the University of Southern California
missionStatement: Our mission is to ignite discovery through education, research and patient care, optimizing health for individuals, our diverse communities and society as a whole.
researchPrograms: The Keck School of Medicine is home to a vibrant scientific community where researchers and clinicians collaborate to create a continuous loop of care – truly embodying the bench to bedside ideal. The Keck School’s rigorous research portfolio spans basic, clinical, translational and population research and utilizes multi-disciplinary collaborations in order to provide solutions for the health problems facing local and international communities.  Medical students have the opportunity to participate in funded summer and year-long research programs, and research electives that meet graduation requirements.
diversity: At the Keck School of Medicine, the Office of Student Engagement and Cultural Affairs (OSECA) is committed to cultivating a campus environment that respects, embraces, and celebrates students of all backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We aim to meaningfully reflect the communities where we live, work, and serve.

shortName: Stanford University School of Medicine
missionStatement:
MD Program Mission Statement
To inspire and prepare a diverse group of exceptional physician scientists, scholars, and leaders to transform human health across all communities through pioneering research and discovery, innovative education, and compassionate patient-centered healthcare.
researchPrograms:
At our research-intensive medical school, students have abundant opportunities to conduct cutting-edge research under the direction of world-class faculty members at the school, hospital and clinics, and throughout the University. For over three decades, the Stanford Medical Scholars Research Program has provided logistical and financial support directly to students, totaling over $3,000,000 this past year, for medical student research on campus and at multiple locations abroad. Research opportunities include diverse areas for student scholarly work, including the basic medical sciences, clinical/translational studies, clinical trials, public health/public policy studies, medical education, medical humanities, and social justice and health equity. For a full list, see:

http://med.stanford.edu/md/student-research/scholarly-concentrations.html
diversity:
Stanford takes pride in its highly diverse and exceptionally qualified student body and welcomes all individuals and groups to pursue a career in medicine. To view programs and groups committed to supporting these efforts including the summer Leadership in Health Disparities Program (LHDP), please visit the Office of Diversity in Medical Education website at https://med.stanford.edu/odme

For information related to ODME programming, contact Mark Gutierrez, Director of ODME at marz@stanford.edu.

shortName: Rutgers New Jersey Medical School
missionStatement:
Mission:
The mission of New Jersey Medical School is to educate students, physicians, and scientists to meet society’s current and future healthcare needs through patient-centered education; pioneering research; innovative clinical, rehabilitative and preventive care; and collaborative community outreach.

Vision:
To create, transmit and utilize knowledge to shape the future of medicine and to enhance the quality of life for the people of New Jersey.

Values:
-Personal respect for patients, students, staff, faculty and community
-Passionate commitment to excellence in service, research and training
-Celebration of diversity in culture, ethnicity, religion, gender and individual goals
-Professionalism in all conduct
-Commitment to serving needs of constituents
-Progress through partnerships
researchPrograms:
Over the past few years, NJMS investigators have secured over $180 million in NIH funding, reflecting steady growth in our research enterprise. Our funding supports critical clinical therapeutic needs across a range of disciplines, including cardiovascular, infectious, inflammatory, neurological, ophthalmologic, and cancer diseases. Many of our faculty members are leaders in their fields and have published in high-impact journals.

NJMS is committed to advancing biomedical knowledge and serves as a premier institution for both research and education. We aim to strengthen research resources, with a particular focus on expanding translational research programs. Our research enterprise has successfully supported a diverse array of sponsored programs, including those funded by federal, state, and private grants. The Office of Research and Sponsored Programs offers a robust infrastructure to facilitate research and related activities.
diversity: At NJMS, we have a long-standing commitment to fostering an inclusive environment that reflects the diversity of our community. Our mission is to develop all students with an emphasis on cultural competency, community service, and humanism in all aspects of medical education. We recognize the importance of a healthcare workforce that mirrors the diversity of our patients, as it enhances both the learning experience and the delivery of high-quality, culturally competent care. Through programs such as the Hispanic Center of Excellence, Health Careers Opportunity Program, Robert Wood Johnson Foundation/AAMC Summer Health Professions Education Program, and our Mini-Medical School, we remain dedicated to recruiting a diverse student body and improving access to care for underserved populations.

shortName: State University of New York Upstate Medical University Alan and Marlene Norton College of Medicine
missionStatement: The primary mission of SUNY Upstate is the education of health professionals and biomedical research. Upstate's clinical faculty and healthcare professionals commit themselves to education and patient care, demonstrating excellence and compassion. In pursuing its mission, Upstate provides its faculty, staff, students, and volunteers an environment of mutual trust and respect, with opportunities to grow personally and professionally and to make a positive difference in the lives of others.
researchPrograms: Upstate offers a formal MD/Ph.D. program for those that are interested. We also offer opportunities for students to obtain research experience throughout their medical education if they so choose.
diversity:
The Norton College of Medicine (COM) of Upstate Medical University commits to creating and sustaining an environment that is equitable, respectful, and free from prejudice for students, faculty, staff, patients, families, and members of our community.

It is our policy to promote a diverse and inclusive campus, through the recruitment of faculty, staff, and students, admissions initiatives, and support programs. We are committed to addressing the shortage of doctors in small communities and rural areas in our region, and in urban underserved communities. We promote the values of diversity and inclusion throughout the mission of the university and in the various functions supporting those missions. Diversity adds value to the learning environment of our students, and we believe it will enhance their commitment to addressing inequities in healthcare.

shortName: Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University
missionStatement:
Mission
Align with our diverse communities to advance medicine and improve health through education, research, training, and development of the next generation of clinicians, educators, and scientists.

Vision
The Lewis Katz School of Medicine will inspire a new standard of excellence in education and research and lead social change in medicine.

At the Katz School of Medicine, our mission and vision call us to serve, discover, and lead. We believe medicine is not only a science but also a promise. A promise to our patients, our communities, and to the next generation of healers and innovators. Together, we create a future where knowledge, compassion, and collaboration improve lives everywhere.

In 2024, the school launched Inspiring Excellence, a five-year strategic plan that charts a big and bold future that harnesses the unlimited potential and passion deeply embedded within the community and honors a long history of valuing and embracing diversity and health equity. Inspiring Excellence reflects Katz’s commitment to shaping the future of health. It centers on aligning with our communities, advancing equity, and raising the bar in medical education and research. Together, these priorities create a powerful framework for lasting social change in medicine.
researchPrograms:
Students learn about research methodology in the MD program and are prepared to engage in research elective experiences available in each phase of the curriculum. Learning about and participating in research is important to nurture a spirit of inquiry and to generate new knowledge that contributes to the health of patients and communities. Students can participate in research activities the summer after first year.

Biomedical research is conducted collaboratively within the school's basic science and clinical departments and research centers. Among the many opportunities, strengths reside in the research areas of Alzheimer's disease, cardiovascular disease, neuroscience, metabolic disease, substance use disorder, lung disease, cancer biology, HIV, and translational medicine. Collaborative investigations among clinical, basic and translational research units provides a rich environment for increasing knowledge to improve health outcomes.
diversity:
For many years, Katz has been among the top medical schools for enrolling and graduating physicians from a broad range of life experiences. Our current student body represents a wide range of cultural, social and economic backgrounds. As the fabric of society becomes more varied, it is critical that we continue to build on our success. 

The Office of Strategic Partnerships in Health, Education & Resources (SPHERE) sponsors ongoing programs, events and activities designed to support and enrich the educational journey of students as they navigate their career paths. These include: pathway programs for high school and college students as well as a summer pre-matriculation program for medical students.

Mini Med School - exposes high school students to opportunities in healthcare.

Medical and Basic Science Scholars Research Program - faculty introduce college students to the research world.

shortName: University of Tennessee Health Science Center College of Medicine
missionStatement:
Transforming lives through collaborative and inclusive education, research/scholarship, clinical care, and public service is the mission of the University of Tennessee Health Science Center.

The College of Medicine aims to improve the health of Tennesseans and our society as a whole by providing an exceptional and nurturing environment for the education of students and physicians, by contributing to advances in medical science, and by providing health services of the highest quality.
researchPrograms:
NIH Medical Student Research Fellowship Program,
Family Medicine Student Research Assistantship Program,
Campbell Foundation Medical Student Research Experience
Summer Cancer Research Program
Department of Otolaryngology Summer Research Fellowships
Pediatric Oncology Education Program (POE)
Department of Anesthesiology Research Fellowship
West Tennessee Regional Forensic Center Medical Student Preceptorship in Forensic Pathology Program
Carolyn L. Kuckein Student Research Fellowship
Collmann Medical Student Educational Endowment - Knoxville
Preclinical Immersion Program - Chattanooga
diversity: The College values diversity in its medical education programs. Individuals from different backgrounds and experiences not only enhance the quality of education for all students, but also translate into graduates who are more effective and better prepared to serve multiple patient populations. UTHSC College of Medicine actively encourages applications from members of groups who are underrepresented in medicine (e.g., students from groups underrepresented in medicine, rural areas, disadvantaged socioeconomic or educational backgrounds, or students with past or present military service). The Committee on Admissions evaluates nonacademic, as well as, academic factors in the selection process, with consideration being given to the unique backgrounds and challenges of these applicants.

shortName: Tufts University School of Medicine
missionStatement:
The mission of Tufts University School of Medicine is to educate a diverse body of students and advance medical knowledge in a dynamic and collaborative environment. We seek to foster the development of dedicated clinicians, scientists, public health professionals, and educators who will have a sustained positive impact on the health of individuals, communities, and the world.

To achieve the goals of our mission statement, our faculty, students and staff demonstrate our commitment to the following core values in all that we do:

Commitment to Excellence
To cultivate a perpetual spirit of inquiry and creativity, leading to outstanding evidence-based health care, rigorous research and scholarship, and inspired teaching.

Commitment to Humanism
To relieve suffering and improve quality of life. To treat all people with compassion, respecting human dignity and autonomy.

Commitment to Social Responsibility
To serve and advocate for all people, especially underserved and vulnerable patients and populations, by addressing social determinants of health, health equity, social justice, and stewardship of social resources.

Commitment to Professionalism
To act in accordance with the highest standards of integrity, demonstrating personal accountability and resilience, collegiality and teamwork, and the pursuit of lifelong learning.

Tufts University School of Medicine embraces diversity in the broadest form, including racial, ethnic, religious, socioeconomic, geographic diversity, as well as diversity in gender and sexual orientation.

We believe that inclusive excellence is an essential practice in the creation of a teaching and learning environment that promotes quality, excellence, and equity as core values among our future physicians, scientists and public health advocates; a workforce equipped with the knowledge and skill needed to address the range of health challenges facing our increasingly diverse patient population and their communities.
researchPrograms: Medical education at Tufts takes place within a vital and growing research community, internationally known for the quality of its basic science and clinical research. The understanding and appreciation of medical research an essential component of the curriculum. Numerous opportunities are available to students for experiences in basic, clinical, and public health research in a variety of laboratories, clinics, and departments at Tufts and its affiliated hospitals, as well as programs at institutions across the US. A large selection of short-term research opportunities is offered to students during the academic year, as well as the summer vacation period between years one and two. Long-term experiences are also available through programs that allow students to specially tailor the research around the regular Tufts curriculum. Students may also interrupt the regular curriculum to focus exclusively on research through the Research Concentration Program.
diversity: Tufts University School of Medicine embraces diversity in the broadest form, including racial, ethnic, religious, socioeconomic, geographic diversity, as well as diversity in gender and sexual orientation. We believe that inclusive excellence is an essential practice in the creation of a teaching and learning environment that promotes quality, excellence, and equity as core values among our future physicians, scientists and public health advocates; a workforce equipped with the knowledge and skill needed to address the range of health challenges facing our increasingly diverse patient population and their communities. To learn more please visit: https://medicine.tufts.edu/administration/multicultural-affairs

shortName: Tulane University School of Medicine
missionStatement: We improve human health and foster healthy communities through discovery and translation of the best science into clinical practice and education; to deliver the highest quality patient care and prepare the next generation of distinguished clinical and scientific leaders.
researchPrograms: TUSOM students have plenty of opportunities available for getting involved in research, which include basic/bench research, clinical/translational research, population/public health research, and medical education research. Strong research programs exist in cardiovascular, lung, kidney and stem cell biology.  Medical students can apply for the Michael DeBakey Honors Program to begin research in their first year and continue throughout medical school.  Also, students can apply for the ASPIRE Summer Research Fellowship for research between their first and second year. However, students can get involved with research at any time during their medical education. For more information regarding student research, visit: https://medicine.tulane.edu/research/student-research
diversity: Tulane University School of Medicine values diversity. Tulane defines diversity broadly to include: persons of color, members of the LGBTQIA community, members of diverse ethnic groups including those typically underrepresented in medicine, members of economically disadvantaged groups, and any others who bring a different perspective to the learning environment. The school of medicine believes in a rich educational experience for all students through the infusion of cultural competency, sensitivity, and attentiveness. Special activities available for, but not limited to, students from groups underrepresented in medicine participate in efforts to advocate for communities within New Orleans through community service, education, and health advocacy projects. This effort will generate conscientious global citizens primed to provide vital medical care to the diverse population in southeastern Louisiana and around the globe, thus advancing health equity.

shortName: Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of Utah
missionStatement:
The Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of Utah serves all people and communities of Utah and the Mountain West by intentionally working to improve individual and community health outcomes and quality of life. This is achieved through excellence in patient care, education, and research by: 
-Purposefully educating physicians, scientists, and health care professionals to ensure compassionate, patient-centered care to all.
-Serving rural and underserved communities by addressing social determinants of health to decrease health disparities among all people.
-Engaging in scholarly research to advance knowledge, innovation, well-being, and health for all people.
-Fostering a culture of respect and community by recognizing outstanding contributions by students, trainees, staff, faculty, and community partners.
researchPrograms:
The summer Medical Student Research Program (MSRP) is a competitive mentored research program. Medical students have the opportunity to work with basic science, clinical science, or health care research investigators. 

Goals are to enhance students' research horizons and develop scientific presentation and writing skills. Students whose projects are selected for support are paid a stipend from an NIH grant for their research activities. Students are expected to present a poster at an annual Research Forum, which their mentors attend and support their trainees. Students may apply for Travel funds to present their research findings at national meetings. Projects are eight weeks in length and students are expected to work approximately 40 hours/week minus release time to attend designated weekly research seminars. There is a monthly stipend paid for the eight week program. For more information, visit https://medicine.utah.edu/medresearch
diversity:
The mission of the Office of Academic Culture and Community is to create a welcoming and respectful environment in academic medicine for people from all backgrounds, actively recruit and fully foster the development of a workforce that reflects our communities.

Our goals:

•	To lead efforts for cultural awareness and embrace and welcome cultural differences in the School of Medicine and the Utah community
•	To maintain educational continuum through medical school
•	To support partnerships within the School of Medicine and the entire Utah community
•	To create sustainable educational and health partnerships throughout the entire Utah community.
•	To embrace all medical students' volunteer efforts to serve the Utah community

shortName: Vanderbilt University School of Medicine
missionStatement:
The School of Medicine is led by a talented and expert team of administrators, staff and faculty who are committed to the success of its people and the advancement of safe, effective, ethical, evidence-based, and patient-centered health care. 

The core values of Vanderbilt University School of Medicine are integrity, belonging, humility, fairness, mutual respect, and excellence.

Our Mission
The mission of Vanderbilt University School of Medicine is to catalyze the advancement of impactful discovery, servant leadership, and lifelong learning.

To carry out this mission, we make these strategic commitments:

*To nurture the growth of clinicians, scientists, and educators who will serve and lead their local, national, and global communities.
*To create, implement, and disseminate new knowledge that expands understanding of health, disease, and healthcare systems.
*To teach, learn, and provide compassionate, personalized caring of the highest quality for every patient who seeks our service and to strive to achieve health for all in the populations we serve. 
*To embrace a culture of lifelong learning, critical thinking, and innovation so that we will continuously improve in all we do.
*To build a broad community of faculty, staff, and students that expands the richness of our learning environment and enhances excellence in all of our endeavors.
researchPrograms: The involvement of medical professionals in the biomedical research enterprise is invaluable due to their position of direct access to patients, evidence-based knowledge of diseases and therapeutics and perspective regarding health systems and the policies that govern. Research education, training and experience is integrated throughout the medical school curriculum in order to cultivate physicians with the knowledge and skill base critical to the clinical practice of medicine, the conduct of biomedical research, and leadership in any arena of medicine. During the Inquiry Program, students participate in research-focused coursework and training in the first two years, and a 1-month project-planning course followed by 3 to 6 months of full-time mentored research during years 3 and/or 4. Students may elect to research in six broad areas: bench, bedside, bioinformatics, community and global health, epidemiology, and ethics, education, policy and society.
diversity: As of 2-28-2025, there are numerous programs to support all students contributing to the diversity of our student body at Vanderbilt University School of Medicine, including the Student National Medical Association, Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association, Methuselah Society (non-trad students), 1GMD (first gen.), Pride in Medicine, and Latino Medical Student Association, to name a few. The Program for LGBTI Health is housed in VUMC ( https://www.vumc.org/lgbtq/ ).

shortName: Robert Larner, M.D., College of Medicine at the University of Vermont
missionStatement:
We celebrate over 200 years of excellence in educating physicians and physician-scientists, and in serving our local and global community.

The mission of the Larner College of Medicine at The University of Vermont is to educate a diverse group of dedicated physicians and biomedical scientists to serve across all the disciplines of medicine; to bring hope to patients by advancing medical knowledge through research; to integrate education and research to advance the quality and accessibility of patient care; and to engage with our communities to benefit Vermont and the world. We achieve this mission through: 

Admissions: Mission aligned 
Mission Aligned Selection and Retention Process: Our applicant screening, interview, and acceptance processes are guided by our mission. Each matriculating student demonstrates excellence in one or more of the specific tenets of our mission, whether through research, experience with rural and disadvantaged communities, or a significant commitment to the betterment of humanity. At the core of our university is a strong mission for social justice, which appears in our medical school's mission. Because we value the unique benefits of social learning, our interview day includes a team-based activity to help our candidates become familiar with this teaching approach.

Student Affairs: Individualized- Timely- Compassionate 
A strong, interdisciplinary, and robust team of student support professionals that "hold" our students as soon as they commit to the first day of Orientation until the day they are hooded and earn their MD. The team includes Personal Health & Well-being, Academic Support, & Intensive Career Planning, spanning both of our campuses. 

Curriculum: Innovative- Learner Centered- Engaging- Relevant
Our active learning approach to instruction is built on adult learning principles and proven educational pedagogy. Our students construct knowledge through a variety of teaching modalities. Larner provides rural and urban clinical opportunities on two campuses in Vermont and Connecticut, where our learners engage with diverse patient populations. Our two-campus model also allows students to select an academic (VT) or community (CT) setting for their clinical rotations. Each student is required to complete a community-focused public health project in their first year, which positions them to learn how to be present in a community, because this is their passion. Check out our website for additional curricular opportunities!

The secret to achieving our mission is our well-defined culture of professionalism. Each student who is admitted to Larner can expect to enter a community that is committed to a culture of professionalism: 
Our Larner College of Medicine community upholds the highest standards of professionalism as we pursue lifelong learning and improvement. We demonstrate professionalism through integrity, accountability, compassion, altruism, and social responsibility. We honor the trust our society has placed in us as stewards of the art and science of medicine, guided by cultural humility, kindness, and respect in our daily interactions. We expect all members of our community to embrace these principles of professionalism as we strive to conduct and support patient care, research, and education that are second to none.
researchPrograms: Students are able to apply for research fellowships in the summer between first and second year of their medical studies. Other research opportunities outside of this internship exist  at the medical school and the larger UVM campus.
diversity:
Our commitment to diversity at the Larner College of Medicine runs deep. We value diversity as a driver of excellence and support the education of physicians and scientists who will go on to serve, and thrive in a multicultural local and global community. We know that in today's society, our future physicians need a level of cultural competence that spans the globe. 

We believe that diversity leads to excellence and is an asset in teaching, research and patient care. These values have implications for our students as they go on to practice: Fostering a community of scholars and clinicians from different backgrounds provides the richest set of viewpoints for decision-making in health care. Our students graduate as culturally competent medical professionals ready for the challenges of ensuring health equity in our global society.

We embrace diversity in its broadest forms, encompassing the intersectionality of identities that define an individual's lived experiences.

shortName: Rutgers, Robert Wood Johnson Medical School
missionStatement:
School Mission: Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is dedicated to transforming health care for New Jersey and the nation through innovation and excellence in education, discovery, patient and family-centered care and addressing the health of our diverse community.

School Vision: Robert Wood Johnson Medical School will become the academic engine driving a new healthcare paradigm in New Jersey; the state's first and largest academic high-value health care system.

School Core Values: Respect, dignity, and humanism for the diverse community we serve and the diverse community we are; Wellness and resilience; Joining learners hand-in-hand with care delivery; Making patients first with safe, compassionate, high-quality care; Science to advance human health.

Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is dedicated to excellence in medical education and to developing ethical and culturally competent physicians. Students are encouraged toward a lifelong commitment to learning and professional growth.

Education Mission:  The medical education program aspires to be a nationally recognized program.  It is a patient-centered program that prepares medical learners to become resilient and adaptable physicians who provide high value, ethical and appropriate healthcare in an ever changing system; communicate respectfully and effectively in a patient and family centered fashion; collaborate with other health care professionals to devise treatment plans and strategies for adherence and self-care, tailored to the needs and preferences of the patient; integrate the scientific underpinnings of clinical medicine and best evidence into daily practice; and who distinguish themselves as medical professionals in discovery, service and leadership.

A key aspect of our mission is having graduates who can provide care “tailored to the needs and preferences of the patient,” and therefore, we recruit and admit students whose experiences and backgrounds can enrich the learning environment and who share a wide range of perspectives. The health equity competency ensures our students understand and can serve the community in which they practice. Our students engage in a wide range of enrichment activities and distinguish themselves in areas such as research, medical education, leadership, climate health, entrepreneurship, global health, humanities, and service to the community, to name a few. They are prepared to practice in a variety of healthcare environments, from the academic medical center to local community hospitals, office practices, federally qualified health centers, and the home. They fulfill the school’s missions by pursuing a wide range of specialties, including primary care. 

Rutgers New Jersey Medical School (NJMS) and Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School (RWJMS) are moving forward with plans to integrate into a unified Future Rutgers School of Medicine, anticipated to launch in the 2027–2028 academic year, pending accreditation by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME). The earliest possible accreditation date is June 2027.
This integration will bring together the strengths of both institutions to create one medical school with two co-equal campuses in Newark and New Brunswick. The future school is designed to become a national leader in academic medicine and health equity—advancing medical education, scientific discovery, patient care, and community service to improve health outcomes for all.
To learn more about the Future Rutgers School of Medicine, please visit:
https://rutgershealth.org/future-school-of-medicine
researchPrograms: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School offers a continuum of research-oriented enrichment programs, including first-year electives and laboratory experiences, summer research training and fellowship opportunities, the Distinction in Research program, MD MS in Clinical and Translational Sciences and MD/PhD Programs, with graduate study in any Rutgers graduate program including humanities or social science. Students can pursue year-long research experiences as Student Scholars.  School research strengths include cancer, neurosciences/neurological diseases, child health, health disparities, cardiovascular,  metabolic and immunological diseases, and the molecular basis of disease.  The plethora of academic strengths of the entire Rutgers community from the humanities to biomedical engineering to population health, affords students the opportunity to realize their full potential in discovery.
diversity:
The Cognitive Skills Program provides academic support to students in all four years of medical school. It provides services to students to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of their study and test-taking strategies. Services are tailored to student's specific needs and integrated with the curriculum.
Careers in Medicine offers support to medical students as they navigate their career paths. Led by Faculty Champions and a dedicated team of trained specialty advisors, students receive personalized guidance at every stage of their journey. 
The THRIVE Curriculum offers regular sessions covering wellbeing, career advising, and equity topics through large group, small group and peer sessions that celebrate our vibrant and diverse Robert Wood Johnson Medical School community. 
The Student Wellness Program assists students in adjusting to the stressors and pressures of medical school. Robert Wood Johnson Medical School provides free, confidential mental health services for students.

shortName: University of Virginia School of Medicine
missionStatement: At the University of Virginia School of Medicine, our mission is to transform health and inspire hope for all Virginians and beyond. Our vision is to be the nation’s leading public academic School of Medicine and the best place to work - while transforming patient care, research, education, and management with the communities we serve.
researchPrograms: The University's research sites around campus are numerous and include the Carter Harrison Research Building, MR4 and MR5 Research Buildings and Fontaine Research Park. The Ivy Translational Research Building offers students translational opportunities. In February 2022 the Ivy Mountain Center for Orthopedics was unveiled. This 200,000 square ft building is considered one of the largest in the nation. National and International Opportunities are available for basic science, social science and clinical research. Recently, a state of the art building devoted to Data Science was unveiled. In late 2026 the new Manning Institute for Biotechnology will serve as an exciting hub for biotechnology. These opportunities occur both during the academic semesters (international clinical rotations occur throughout the year), summer or other holidays, as well as during their elective time.
diversity: The University of Virginia offers over 100 student groups through the Mulholland Society. There are strong outreach programs in the community connected to these student groups.

shortName: Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine
missionStatement: Our mission is to improve health through exceptional and innovative discovery, training and patient care. With the help of our strategic plan, we will achieve our vision of being known for the accomplishments of our trainees, faculty, staff and alumni in research, education and patient care.
researchPrograms: While students are not required to participate in research or write a thesis as a graduation requirement, the vast majority participate in some type of research experience prior to graduation. More information about research for medical students can be found here: https://medschool.vcu.edu/research/medical-students/

shortName: University of Washington School of Medicine
missionStatement:
The UWSOM is dedicated to improving the general health and well-being of the public. As the pre-eminent academic medical center in our region and as a national leader in biomedical research, we place special emphasis on educating and training physicians, scientists, and allied health professionals dedicated to two distinct missions:
- Meeting the health care needs of our region, especially by recognizing the importance of primary care and providing service to underserved populations; 
- Advancing knowledge and assuming leadership in the biomedical sciences and in academic medicine.
The School has a special responsibility to the people in the states of WA, WY, AK, MT, and ID. We are committed to building and sustaining a multi-faceted academic community and to assuring that access to education and training is open to learners from all segments of society. http://www.uwmedicine.org/education/about/mission
researchPrograms: Since 1974 UW School of Medicine has ranked consistently among the top 3 schools in receipt of National Institutes of Health (NIH) grant funding. There are numerous opportunities for students to participate in research. Students involved in the Medical Scientist Research Training Program (MSRTP) could be eligible for housing and travel support.
diversity:
UWSOM is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse learning environment for all students and training culturally competent physicians to care for the region's increasingly diverse population. We have programs designed to train medical students to support urban, rural, and global underserved populations, and many students engage in student-led service learning and community outreach to address health disparities. 
Our Equity & Medical Student Engagement team is committed to supporting students to become health-equity minded physicians.
The Office of Health Care Equity (OHCE) supports student programming that promote diversity and excellence in medical education, e.g., Pathways Programs, the Center for Restorative Practices, and Anti-bias/anti-racism training.

shortName: Washington University in St. Louis School of Medicine
missionStatement:
In leading the advancement of human health, WashU Medicine will:
Cultivate excellence and collegiality within an equitable and inclusive community.
Attract, develop, advance and support a diverse and talented current and future workforce.
Innovate through discoveries and inventions in basic, clinical, translational and population sciences.
Build and support an environment that fosters exceptionally creative research, health care, education and the well-being of our workforce.
Use our academic excellence and scientific rigor to continually advance and enhance health care in a way that ensures access, compassion, high value, equity and evidence-based care for all people in our community, including those who are underserved and uninsured.
Observe the highest standards of ethics, integrity and humanity across all of our missions.
Apply advances in research, education and health care for the betterment of the human condition, locally and globally.

Educating tomorrow’s leaders in biomedicine involved reimagining a medical curriculum that fosters both self-directed and team-based learning.
